statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail risk is low with no tradable session in progress.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The 22:00 UTC Globex reopen and Monday's 13:30 UTC US cash open are the evidence checkpoints at which the conditional allowance in the forecast is either confirmed or retired. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Weekend Globex halt keeps Tail low while a 5% ten-year and $100 crude hold Stress moderate
body: The last cash session was Friday 18 September, when the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, in a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range, with VIX at 14.81 and the ten-year Treasury yield finishing at 4.998% after trading above 5% intraweek for the first time since July 2007. That close sat near the session high, but it coincided with a very large quarterly expiry, so it is treated as expiry mechanics rather than directional evidence. The macro backdrop is unusually loaded: the FOMC raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, the first increase in more than three years, and the effective funds rate printed 3.88% on 17 September. Crude remains elevated, with WTI at $100.30 and Brent at $103.87, though both fell for a third consecutive session on Friday as Saudi Arabia rerouted exports through the Strait of Hormuz and guided to roughly half East-West pipeline capacity within days and full service in about six weeks. No new Gulf escalation has been verified over the weekend. CME Globex is halted until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path is observable and no persistent one-way structure can be established; Tail therefore stays low. Stress is moderate and reflects the rate, energy and geopolitical backdrop rather than any observed price path. The conditional risk is concentrated at the Sunday reopen, where thin liquidity could extend a weekend gap before two-way flow returns, and secondarily at Monday's US cash open. A reported but officially unconfirmed Trump-Xi meeting around 24 September sits in the week ahead as a headline variable and is not carried in the verified event calendar.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 clock-hours the published Claude assessment was continuously green with the EA_ON mapping and a normal dominant mode. Tail held in a narrow 4-5 range, confirming that no persistent one-way structure was identified at any point. Stress drifted up from 24 during Friday's late US session to 30-31 through the Saturday and Sunday hours and 33 most recently, tracking the rate and energy backdrop rather than any observed price path, while confidence stayed in a 71-76 band on consistent evidence quality.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours divide into three phases. Five further halted hours carry Tail at 5-7, where the reading is informational rather than structural. The 22:00 UTC Globex reopen opens a narrow danger window to 01:00 UTC, with Tail conditionally raised to 10-13 for thin-liquidity gap-and-extend risk; this is an allowance for an unobserved path and would decay quickly on an orderly reopen with a visible retracement. Asian and European hours then normalise toward Tail 9-10 on a light Monday calendar whose only scheduled item is the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed National Activity Index, before a secondary conditional peak of 12-13 around the 13:30 UTC US cash open. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and Stress stays moderate at 33-44 throughout on the unchanged 5% yield, $100 crude and hawkish Fed backdrop.

forecast.analysis: Globex is halted through this hour, so no live NQ path exists and mean reversion cannot be tested; Tail stays low because no one-way structure is observable. Friday's cash close was orderly at NDX 29,644.17, +0.67%, with VIX 14.81. Stress carries the 5% ten-year, $100 WTI and the unresolved Saudi outage.
drivers: CME Globex halted until 22:00 UTC; no live NQ price path is testable this hour
Ten-year ended Friday at 4.998% after topping 5% intraweek, highest since Jul 2007
WTI $100.30 (-1.58%), Brent $103.87 on a third straight lower session
Fed hiked 25bp on Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%; effective funds rate 3.88% on Sep 17

forecast.analysis: A further halted hour adds no price-path evidence, so the published Tail stays informational rather than structural. Stress ticks up only because the reopen draws nearer against an unchanged backdrop: Saudi Arabia is guiding to roughly half East-West capacity within days and full service in about six weeks, leaving the outage live but narrowing.
drivers: Halt continues; no incremental NQ structure can accrue during this hour
Saudi guidance: about half pipeline capacity within days, full service in six weeks
Weekend headlines are the only transmission channel while futures are shut

news.title: Oil Extends Slump as Saudi Arabia Moves to Restore Key Pipeline

forecast.analysis: Still halted, so Tail remains an allowance rather than a reading. The standing amplifier for this hour is the Hormuz tanker war, which has run since February and is the mechanism by which a weekend headline could reprice crude before equities can respond. No new escalation has been verified since Friday's close.
drivers: No verified new Hormuz or Iran escalation since Friday's cash close
Tanker-war backdrop is persistent, not a fresh discontinuity this weekend
Crude is the fastest weekend transmission path into Monday index pricing

news.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?

forecast.analysis: Two hours before the reopen, Tail is nudged only to reflect that the halt window is closing, not because structure has been seen. The conditional mechanism to watch is mechanical: a Sunday reopen prints into thin books, so an initial imbalance can travel further per contract than the same order flow would move price in cash hours.
drivers: Thin reopen books can amplify an initial imbalance before two-way flow returns
Any gap would be a liquidity artefact first and a directional signal only later
Tail rise here is a countdown allowance, not observed one-way structure

forecast.analysis: The final halted hour. Tail and Stress are set for what the reopen could bring rather than for anything observed: the gap reference is Friday's 29,644.17 settlement, and the conditional risk is that a wide opening print extends before a first retracement appears. Nothing in the verified weekend record yet supports that path.
drivers: Gap reference for the 22:00 UTC reopen is Friday's NDX settlement 29,644.17
Conditional risk is extension before a first retracement, not a level being reached
Saudi pipeline shut since Sep 11 remains the main unresolved supply catalyst

news.title: Oil prices rise after Saudi Arabia shuts down critical pipeline that bypasses Strait of Hormuz

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens and the mapped danger window opens with it. Tail is conditionally raised for thin-liquidity gap-and-extend risk during the first prints; this is an allowance for an unobserved path, not a claim that a gap has occurred. It would decay quickly if the reopen is orderly and an early retracement is visible.
drivers: 22:00 UTC Globex reopen begins the mapped danger window to 01:00 UTC
Conditional checkpoint: does a first meaningful retracement appear in the opening hour
Sunday-evening depth is at its thinnest, so slippage risk exceeds direction risk

news.title: Stock market next week: Outlook for Sept. 21-25, 2026

forecast.analysis: First full hour of restored trade. The conditional test is whether the opening imbalance is absorbed: repeated extension after a failed pullback would be genuine Tail evidence, while a two-sided range would retire most of the reopen allowance. Tail eases slightly because the thinnest liquidity pocket is by then behind the session.
drivers: Conditional invalidation: repeated extension after a failed pullback would raise Tail
Absorption of the opening imbalance would retire most of the reopen allowance
Thinnest liquidity pocket sits in the first prints, not this hour

forecast.analysis: Handover toward Asia. Tail continues to step down on the assumption that price discovery has been orderly; if instead NQ were holding near a session extreme with shallow pullbacks, this slot would understate the risk and the next assessment would correct it. Stress stays moderate on the unchanged rate and energy backdrop.
drivers: Asian handover normally restores two-way flow and supports mean reversion
Conditional flag: NQ holding near a session extreme would invalidate this decay
Rate and energy backdrop is unchanged, so Stress does not decay with Tail

forecast.analysis: The mapped danger window closes at this instant. Beyond it, the reopen allowance is retired and Tail reverts toward the overnight baseline, conditional on the evening having produced visible retracements. Crude reopening alongside equities is the cross-asset checkpoint, given WTI's third consecutive lower session into Friday.
drivers: Danger window ends 01:00 UTC; reopen allowance is retired from this slot
Cross-asset checkpoint: crude direction on the reopen after three lower sessions
Baseline overnight Tail assumes retracements were visible during the evening

news.title: Oil prices fall as Saudi Arabia reportedly offers more crude via Hormuz after pipeline attack

forecast.analysis: Tokyo is in its opening stretch. Overnight Asian hours historically give the reverse strategy its most reliable mean reversion because ranges compress and directional conviction is low. Tail is held near baseline on that structural expectation rather than on any observed Monday price path, which does not yet exist.
drivers: Asian hours typically compress range and favour mean reversion over trend
No Monday price path is observed at assessment time; this slot is conditional
Yen and JGB tone are the regional read-across to watch for a rate shock

forecast.analysis: Asian mid-session, the quietest part of the 24-hour cycle for NQ. Tail sits at its forecast low. The standing conditional risk is a headline out of the Gulf during Asian hours, when depth is thin enough that a crude repricing can carry into index futures before European desks arrive to take the other side.
drivers: Quietest liquidity phase for NQ; forecast Tail sits at its cycle low
Conditional risk: a Gulf headline repricing crude before European depth returns
East-West pipeline remains the single largest unresolved supply variable

news.title: Why Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline matters for global oil

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hours. Stress eases marginally as the reopen is fully behind and no scheduled US release falls in this window. The persistent driver is the policy backdrop: the Fed's first hike in over three years landed on Sep 16 and the dot plot carried one further increase in 2026, which keeps a higher-for-longer discount under index multiples.
drivers: Fed's Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% keeps a higher-for-longer discount on multiples
Dot plot carried one further 2026 increase; futures price roughly 42% odds of two
No scheduled US release falls in this hour, so event risk is headline-only

news.title: September Fed Meeting: Updates and Commentary

forecast.analysis: Asian close approaches with no scheduled catalyst. Tail stays at baseline on the conditional assumption that the overnight session has been two-sided. Confidence is capped rather than low, because the level, rate, energy and calendar evidence behind this slot is verified while the price path for it is necessarily unobserved.
drivers: No scheduled catalyst in this hour; risk is carry-over and headline only
Confidence capped by an unobserved forward path, not by thin current evidence
Baseline holds only if the overnight session has been genuinely two-sided

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Depth begins rebuilding as London and Frankfurt desks arrive, which normally improves rather than degrades mean reversion. Tail is unchanged at baseline. The conditional checkpoint is whether the overnight range holds into the European cash open or is broken on the first wave of European flow.
drivers: European desks rebuild depth, which normally supports mean reversion
Conditional checkpoint: does the overnight range hold into the European cash open
A clean range break on first European flow would argue for a higher Tail

forecast.analysis: European cash markets open. Tail is nudged up a point for the session-transition effect, in which a fresh pool of directional flow can briefly extend the overnight range. This is a recurring structural allowance rather than a forecast that the range will break, and it typically unwinds within the first European hour.
drivers: European cash open introduces fresh directional flow at a session transition
Transition allowance typically unwinds inside the first European hour
Energy complex reopens in Europe, re-linking crude to index pricing

forecast.analysis: First full European hour. The conditional test repeats at a different venue: an orderly two-way European open would confirm the low-Tail path, while shallow pullbacks and repeated extension would be the first genuine one-way evidence of the new week. Crude direction in European trade is the cross-asset tell.
drivers: Conditional test: two-way European trade confirms the low-Tail path
Shallow pullbacks plus repeated extension would be first one-way evidence this week
European crude pricing is the cross-asset tell for the equity open

news.title: Oil Extends Slump as Saudi Arabia Moves to Restore Key Pipeline

forecast.analysis: European mid-morning. Tail returns to baseline as the open-transition allowance decays. The unchanged macro frame still dominates Stress: a ten-year at 5%, crude at $100 and a Fed that has just turned, a combination that has produced elevated volatility without, so far, producing the no-retracement path that Tail actually measures.
drivers: Open-transition allowance decays; Tail returns to the European baseline
5% ten-year plus $100 crude keeps Stress elevated without implying one-way price
Friday's tape absorbed the rate backdrop rather than trending away from it

forecast.analysis: European late morning, with no US release yet in the window. This slot carries the lowest conditional risk of the European block. The main forward-looking consideration is positioning into the US session, where the first scheduled data point of the week arrives at 12:30 UTC and the cash open follows at 13:30 UTC.
drivers: Lowest conditional risk of the European block; no scheduled release in window
Positioning begins to build toward the 12:30 UTC and 13:30 UTC checkpoints
No verified catalyst is scheduled between now and the US premarket

forecast.analysis: European midday into the US premarket. Stress edges up as the session with real event risk approaches, while Tail holds at baseline because approaching an event is not itself evidence of a pathological path. That distinction is deliberate: event importance and dispersion belong in Stress until price actually behaves one-way.
drivers: Approaching event risk lifts Stress; it is not by itself evidence for Tail
US premarket begins to form the reference range for the cash open
Chicago Fed National Activity Index for August is due at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for August prints at 12:30 UTC, a medium-impact release that rarely moves the index on its own but sets the tone for a data-light Monday. Tail is nudged for the release window; Stress rises more, consistent with treating scheduled events as a volatility rather than a path risk.
drivers: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (Aug) at 12:30 UTC is a medium-impact checkpoint
Monday's calendar is light; the week's high-impact print is Wednesday's flash PMIs
Release windows are scored into Stress first and Tail only on observed behaviour

forecast.analysis: The US cash open at 13:30 UTC is the week's first real liquidity event and the secondary conditional peak in this forecast. Tail is raised for opening-auction continuation risk, the pattern in which an aligned open extends with shallow pullbacks. Whether it applies is unobservable now and must be scored from the actual auction.
drivers: 13:30 UTC US cash open is the secondary conditional peak in this forecast
Opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific Tail pattern
Applicability is unobservable now and must be scored from the actual auction

forecast.analysis: First full US cash hour and the forecast peak. Tail sits at 13 on the conditional combination of a hawkish Fed, a 5% ten-year and $100 crude meeting new-week positioning. It remains well below the block threshold because no amplifier is currently observed, only anticipated, and anticipation is scored into Stress.
drivers: Forecast Tail peak on conditional new-week positioning into an aligned macro frame
Amplifiers are anticipated rather than observed, so Tail stays below the threshold
Rate, energy and policy backdrop unchanged since Friday's verified close

forecast.analysis: US late morning. Tail eases as the opening auction resolves and intraday liquidity is at its deepest, which historically restores the retracements the strategy depends on. The conditional invalidation remains explicit: NQ holding near a session extreme with failed retracements would argue for a higher reading than this slot carries.
drivers: Deepest intraday liquidity historically restores the retracements Tail measures
Conditional invalidation: session-extreme holding with failed retracements
Crude remains the live cross-asset variable while the pipeline stays partly shut

forecast.analysis: US midday closes this forecast horizon. Tail decays toward the low-teens on the expectation of orderly two-way trade, and the next assessments will replace every conditional slot here with observed evidence. Stress stays moderate because the rate, energy and geopolitical frame is not resolved by a single orderly session.
drivers: Horizon end; conditional slots will be replaced by observed evidence hourly
Midday decay assumes orderly two-way trade rather than asserting it
Rate, energy and Gulf frame persists beyond any single orderly session
